minutes_text:
Inglewood, California
  March 8, 2022

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
March 8, 2022, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:01 p.m.
The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:
  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales
  and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEM. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on the
Closed Session Item.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:01 p.m. for Closed Session Item
No. CS-1.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the
hour of 2:03 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.
PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
item on the Agendas, other than the public hearing.
Gregory Esry spoke concerning an issue that he had regarding registering his apartment
units with the Housing Protection Department.

  1
 March 8, 2022

 125  RESOLUTION NO. 22-58 ADOPTED – AUTHORIZING THE CITY COUNCIL
  AND ALL OTHER LEGISLATIVE BODIES THE CONTIUANCE TO CONDUCT
  PUBLIC MEETINGS VIA TELECONFERENCE FROM MARCH 8, 2022,
  THROUGH APRIL 7, 2022, PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361. Staff report
  dated March 8, 2022, was presented recommending the adoption of a resolution
  authorizing the City Council, and all other legislative bodies of the City, to continue to
  conduct public meetings via teleconference from March 8, 2022, through April 7, 2022,
  pursuant to Assembly Bill 361.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  Resolution No. 22-58 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA AUTHORIZING THE CITY COUNCIL
  AND ALL OTHER LEGISLATIVE BODIES TO CONTINUE TO
  CONDUCT PUBLIC MEETINGS VIA TELECONFERENCE FROM
  MARCH 8, 2022, THROUGH APRIL 7, 2022 PURSUANT TO AB 361.

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  March 3, 2022, in the amount of $4,017,621.56 are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 131.8  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – REVISED DRAFT FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021
  CONSOLIDATED ANNUAL PERFORMANCE EVALUATION REPORT
  (CAPER) APPROVED. The City Clerk announced the next scheduled matter was a
  public hearing to consider approval of the revised DRAFT 2020 Consolidated Annual
  Performance Evaluation Report (CAPER) for Fiscal Year 2020-2021 for resubmission to
  the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), notice had been given
  in the time, form, and manner as required by law, an affidavit was on file and
  communications were received, and passed out to the Mayor and City Council Members.

  Artie Fields, City Manager presented the staff report dated March 8, 2022.

  Roberto Chavez, HUD Programs Manager gave a brief overview.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on this matter.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on Agenda Item No. DR-1, Adoption of a
  resolution authorizing the City Council, and all other legislative bodies the continuance to
  conduct public meetings via teleconference from March 8, 2022, through April 7, 2022,
  pursuant to Assembly Bill 361. She also questioned how much of the CDBG Funds for
  the COVID 19 Rent Relief was left.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on the CBDG Funds and asked for clarification
  regarding the rest of the funds. She also stated she has been on the waiting list since
  2019, and the Housing Advisor told her it was a separate list for the COVID 19 Rent
  Relief funds. She requested information on how to apply for the COVID 19 Rent Relief.

  2
 March 8, 2022

  Mayor Butts closed the public comment portion at the hour of 2:20 p.m.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby approve the revised DRAFT 2020 Consolidated Annual
  Performance Evaluation Report for Fiscal Year 2020-2021. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 132  CLAIM DENIED. Letter from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claim Pursuant to Government Code Section 913:
  1) Annabelle Jones for alleged property damage; tree roots on September 29, 2021.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby reject claim listed as A-1. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 171  GRANT AGREEMENT NO. 22-156 APPROVED – CITY OF INGLEWOOD AND
  LOS ANGELES DODGERS FOUNDATION; RESOLUTION NO. 22-59
  ADOPTED – AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2021-2022 ANNUAL BUDGET.
  Staff report dated March 8, 2022, was presented recommending approval of a grant
  agreement between the City of Inglewood and Los Angeles Dodgers Foundation for the
  Dodgers Dreamteam Program.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Grant Agreement No. 22-156; and 2)
  Adopt Resolution No. 22-59 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2021-2022 ANNUAL
  BUDGET TO ACCEPT GRANT FUNDS FROM THE LOS ANGELES
  DODGERS FOUNDATION FOR STAFFING, FIELD MAINTENANCE,
  AND  UMPIRE FEES FOR THE YEAR 2022 DODGERS
  DREAMTEAM PROGRAM

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 183  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – OMEGA EVENTS, INC. (OMEGA). Staff report
  dated March 8, 2022, was presented recommending authorization of payment of Invoice
  No. 3037 submitted by Omega Events, Inc. (Omega), for additional production and
  backline equipment items needed by the Stage Contractor for the Taste of Inglewood Big
  Game Concert Series Festival.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby authorized payment in the amount of $24,363.85. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 131.9  PUBLIC HEARING SET – EXTENDING THE INTERIM ORDINANCE
  ADOPTED FEBRUARY 1, 2022. Staff report dated March 8, 2022, was presented
  recommending that a public hearing be set to extend the interim ordinance adopted on
  February 1, 2022.

  Mayor Butts set the public hearing for March 15, 2022, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.; and

  3
 March 8, 2022

  Mayor Butts ordered the report pertaining to the establishment of a permanent short-term
  rental ordinance in the City of Inglewood received and filed.

 132.6  CLOSED SESSION – CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR; SERVICE
  EMPLOYEES  INTERNATIONAL  UNION  (SEIU);  INGLEWOOD
  MANAGEMENT EMPLOYEE ORGANIZATION (IMEO); INGLEWOOD
  POLICE CIVILIAN MANAGEMENT ASSOCIATION (IPCMA); INGLEWOOD
  POLICE OFFICERS ASSOCIATION (IPOA); INGLEWOOD POLICE
  MANAGEMENT ASSOCIATION (IPMA); AND INGLEWOOD EXECUTIVE
  ORGANIZATION (IEO). Closed Session – Confidential – Attorney/Client Privileged;
  Conference with Labor Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6; Name
  of the Agency Negotiator: Jose O. Cortes, Human Resources Director; Name of
  Organizations Representing Employees: Service Employees International Union (SEIU);
  Inglewood Management Employee Organization (IMEO); Inglewood Police Civilian
  Management Association (IPCMA); Inglewood Police Officer Association (IPOA);
  Inglewood Police Management Association (IPMA); and Inglewood Executive
  Organization (IEO).

  Discussion Held; Direction Given to Staff.

 126  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. City Clerk Aisha L. Thompson wished all women a
  Happy International Women’s Day and read a quote in tribute to women. She reminded
  residents that the third redistricting public hearing will be held on March 15, 2022, at
  2:00 p.m., and all draft maps were due to the City Clerk by March 10, 2022, at 10:00 a.m.
  She also reminded residents that the Special Primary Election for State Assembly District
  62 will be held on April 5, 2022.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) asked if he and his team could schedule a meeting to discuss
  the installation of Solar Systems on the Library and other city buildings. He stated that
  other cities have benefited from the Solar System installation, and the State of California
  will push towards clean and renewable energy by 2045. He also stated that he spoke with
  the Library Manager who was also interested in moving towards clean, and renewable
  energy.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned at the hour of 2:33 p.m.

  Approved this 22nd day of March, 2022

  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
